_provenance.subject: electric vehicles (climate / energy)
_provenance.source: Prism public API — research.evidence (one call per angle)
_provenance.note: Counts and shares measured from the data. Quoted findings verbatim and verified. Every angle formed a real both-sides lane (122-2,391 papers) — no thin lanes here; the story is the verdict, not the depth. Note the mixed valence: 'battery cost' and 'grid strain' are caveat-claims, so a large supporting share there means the caveat is well-evidenced.

angles.claim: electric vehicles reduce greenhouse gas emissions
angles.reading: mixed framing with no dominant lean
angles.note: the solid core — supporting outnumbers contradicting 48:1; lifecycle studies confirm the reduction across vehicle types
evidence: "the transition from internal combustion engine vehicles ... to electric vehicles would reduce the greenhouse gas emission for passenger cars, two-wheelers, and buses" (LCA, Malaysia, Sustainability 2022)
"BEVs have lower CO2 emissions" vs conventional vehicles (Clean Technologies 2023)

angles.claim: electric vehicle battery production has a high environmental cost
angles.reading: mostly positive framing, with a substantial cautionary minority
angles.note: a real, well-studied cost — but a partial offset, not a reversal; the landmark LCA puts the battery at ~15% of total e-mobility impact
evidence: "The share of the total environmental impact of E-mobility caused by the battery ... is 15%" (Notter, Environ. Sci. Technol. 2010)
cradle-to-gate Global Warming Potential 67.1 kg CO2e/kWh for an Indian LFP pack (2025)

angles.claim: electric vehicle adoption strains the electricity grid
angles.reading: overwhelmingly positive framing, which on a citation-weighted corpus can mean consensus or can mean publication bias
angles.note: the one place framing and read-evidence diverge: 454 papers frame EVs as a grid strain, but the high-tier documents read lean CONTRADICT (6 vs 3) — smart charging keeps voltage within limits even at 90% penetration
evidence: "voltage profiles maintained within safe operational limits, even under 90% EV penetration level" (Glasgow, 2025)
"minimal impact on voltage profiles" (Rwanda MV networks, 2020)
counter: "higher line loading, voltage fluctuations, and increased power losses" (37-bus study, 2025)

angles.claim: electric vehicles are cheaper to own than gasoline cars
angles.reading: mostly positive framing, with a substantial cautionary minority
angles.note: conditional — no contradicting papers, but the reads say 'it depends': on segment, mileage, battery replacement and policy
evidence: "the optimal vehicle drive technology depends strongly on the vehicle segment considered" (Applied Energy 2025)
"EVs have a lower TCO ... if the battery replacement cost for EVs is not considered" (Romania study, 2024)

angles.claim: electric vehicles reduce urban air pollution
angles.reading: mostly positive framing, with a substantial cautionary minority
angles.note: the only angle where qualifying (43) outnumbers supporting (36) — benefits depend on the grid mix and can even be regressive
evidence: "people in census block groups with median income greater than about $65,000 receive positive environmental benefits while those below this threshold receive negative environmental benefits" (Holland, JAERE 2018)
support: heavy-duty electrification "consistently improves air quality in terms of NO2 and fine particulate matter" (China, 2020)

stance_composition_pct.what: share of papers that support / qualify / contradict each stated claim (note mixed valence — two claims are caveats), normalised to 100%
